issues.body:
## Summary / user outcome

Let a customer paste several event links at once in the studio intake (`/` and `/make`), check which ones are usable, and turn every valid link into a stub in one batch. Today they have to paste, wait for printing, and come back for each event.

**Priority:** P2. Post-v1 enhancement.
**Required for v1:** No.
**Issue key:** new (GT key pending triage).
**Owner role:** Product and frontend (intake UX and API). Individual assignee pending triage.

## Context / exact gap

Current intake at [main 3ded858](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/tree/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9) handles exactly one link:

- [`StudioStart`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/customer/start/StudioStart.tsx#L233-L262) renders a single-line `<input type="text" inputMode="url">`. Its `onPaste` handler trims the clipboard text and passes it to [`landLink`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/customer/start/StudioStart.tsx#L132), which auto-submits only when the whole string passes `looksLikeLink`.
- [`looksLikeLink` / `inputFromText`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/customer/start/make.ts#L19-L28) treat any text that is not one link as a **search query**. A pasted list of links therefore does not auto-print. If the customer submits it, it is sent as `{ query }` and either searches demo fixtures or is refused once it exceeds `INTAKE_LIMITS.queryChars` (200). The customer is never told that the paste contained links.
- [`POST /api/research`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L489) explicitly refuses a `urls` field ([`UNSUPPORTED_FIELDS`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/server/intake-url.ts#L30)) with "Paste one event page link instead". The 8 KiB body cap covers a single request.
- Link validation ([`parseIntakeUrl` / `checkUrl`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/server/intake-url.ts#L145-L170)) is server-only. It rejects links that are too long (>2048), malformed, non-http(s), contain credentials, use non-standard ports, or point to private/reserved destinations, and it reads bare `example.com/x` as https.

[GT-03 #11](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/11) (closed) defined URL-first single-event intake, including "count/length/scheme rules, duplicate handling and per-field errors". It did not cover creating many stubs from one paste. [#60](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/60) covers batch creation from a connected mailbox, which is a different source. #60 should reuse the batch progress and state model from this issue rather than build its own. No existing issue covers bulk link pasting.

## Scope

- **Multi-link entry.** Offer a multi-line entry (for example, an expanding textarea or a "Paste several links" mode) beside the existing single-link field. A single pasted link keeps the current paste → land → auto-print behaviour unchanged.
- **Parsing.** Split pasted text on newlines (`\n`, `\r\n`) and trim each line. Ignore blank lines. Decide whether whitespace- or comma-separated links on one line are also split, and document the choice. Never treat a multi-link paste as one search query.
- **Validation.** Check each entry with the same rules as `parseIntakeUrl` (scheme, credentials, port, length, private/reserved host, bare-host → https). Share the logic or mirror it client-side so customers get feedback before anything is sent. The server still validates every link independently.
- **Deduplication.** Remove duplicates within the paste after normalisation (scheme added, host lowercased, trailing slash and fragment ignored). Also flag links that already have a stub on the wall/account (see `existingStub`) and offer to reopen those rather than reprint.
- **Invalid entries shown clearly.** List each rejected line with its original text, line number and a specific reason from the existing `URL_REFUSAL` wording (too long, not http/https, has a username/password, unsupported port, not a public event page, unreadable). Invalid lines do not block valid ones, and the customer can edit or remove them inline.
- **Batch add.** Let the customer review the count of valid links and start them in one action. Each valid link goes through the existing research → printing → `keepStubResult` flow and lands on the wall. Agree with the research owner whether the batch runs as sequential single-link `/api/research` calls or through a new batch contract. If a batch contract is added, the `urls` refusal and the body limit change deliberately, not as a side effect.
- **Progress.** Show per-link progress, overall progress and a summary at the end (created, reopened, failed). One failure does not stop the rest. Failed links can be retried without reprinting the ones that already succeeded.
- **Limits.** Set and display a maximum number of links per batch. Existing generation budgets and demo-mode behaviour still apply to every link. In demo mode, links that are not fixtures still produce the existing demo or refusal behaviour, never a fabricated researched result.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On `/` and `/make`, pasting newline-separated links (LF and CRLF, with blank lines and surrounding spaces) yields a parsed list with one row per link. Pasting a single link still auto-prints exactly as it does today.
- [ ] A multi-link paste is never sent to `/api/research` as `{ query }`, and is never silently truncated.
- [ ] Each row is labelled valid or invalid using rules equivalent to `parseIntakeUrl`. Synthetic cases include `ftp://`, `javascript:`, `https://user:pw@…`, `:8080`, `localhost`, `10.0.0.1`, a link longer than 2048 characters, a bare `ticketmaster.com/event/…`, and text that is not a link.
- [ ] Invalid rows show the original text, line number and a specific human reason. Valid rows stay in place while invalid rows are edited or removed. Errors are announced accessibly (associated with the field and announced by a live region) and can be reached by keyboard.
- [ ] Duplicates within the paste collapse to one entry, and the UI shows how many were removed. A link that already has a stub on the wall is flagged and reopened rather than researched again.
- [ ] One "Add N links" action starts all valid links. Every valid link ends with a stub on the wall (or reopens an existing one) through the existing flow. Per-link and overall states (queued, researching, done, reopened, failed) are visible. A failed link can be retried alone.
- [ ] Pastes above the batch limit are refused with a clear message and allow the customer to trim the list. Batch limits and existing per-stub budgets are enforced on the server, not only in the UI.
- [ ] The server still validates each link before dispatch. Unless a batch contract is deliberately agreed and implemented, `urls` remains refused. Rejected links are never fetched and are not echoed into logs (consistent with `intakeRefusal`).
- [ ] Analytics `flow` events cover a bulk paste and its outcome (counts only, no URLs), alongside the existing `intake_paste` and `intake_submit` events.
- [ ] Works on phone and desktop (see [GT-11 #18](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/18)) and with reduced motion.

## Dependencies / related work

- Related: [intake #11](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/11), [email batch import #60](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/60) (share the batch model), [progress/errors #17](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/17), [accessibility #18](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/18), [lifecycle #10](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/10).
- Any change to batch dispatch or limits needs agreement with event-intelligence (safe retrieval, [event-intelligence #9](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence/issues/9)) and the intake contract owner ([shared-contracts #15](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/15)).
- Master acceptance IDs: N/A. This is a new post-v1 feature, and its mapping is pending triage.

## Validation plan / evidence required

Planned checks:

- Unit tests for the parser, normaliser and deduplicator.
- An extension of [`tests/intake-boundaries.test.mjs`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/tests/intake-boundaries.test.mjs) that keeps client and server validation equivalent.
- Route tests for the chosen dispatch path, covering the limit, partial failure and retry.
- A fixture-mode browser run on `/make`: paste a mixed list (valid, invalid, duplicate, existing stub), fix one row, add the batch and confirm the wall contents.

Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build`. Before closure, attach the PR, the tested commit, command results and a sanitized walkthrough. Creating this issue does not claim implementation or passing tests.
issues.title: [Post deployment][P2] Paste several event links at once and create their stubs in one batch

issues.body:
## Summary / user outcome

Recognise Luma event links (`luma.com` and the legacy `lu.ma` domain) as a supported event source. A customer who pastes a Luma link should get a stub with the right event name, dates, place (or "Online"), hosts and status. A Luma link that is not a single event, or that is private to one guest, should get a specific, useful refusal instead of a generic or wrong result.

**Priority:** P2. Post-v1 enhancement.
**Required for v1:** No.
**Issue key:** new (GT key pending triage).
**Owner role:** Product and frontend (research route), coordinating with event-intelligence on the source-support matrix. Individual assignee pending triage.

## Geographic coverage (verified 2026-10-14)
<!-- geo-coverage:2026-10-14 -->

**Luma: International including US.** Regions evidenced: North America (US, Canada, Mexico) evidenced by city lists; region headings also exist for South America, Europe, Asia & Pacific and Africa (their city lists not confirmed).

- **Official sources:** [luma.com/discover](https://luma.com/discover)
- **Evidence:** Discover page lists New York, San Francisco, Toronto, Montréal, Vancouver and Mexico City under North America, with headings for the other regions.

Coverage is taken from the providers' own sites, help centres or country domains, checked 2026-10-14. It is not inferred from headquarters. Regions not listed are **unknown**, not excluded. Evidence marked as a snippet was seen through search-indexed copies of official pages because the site blocks direct requests. Priority is unchanged: **P2**, post-v1 / nice to have; **Required for v1:** No.

## Context / exact gap

At [main 3ded858](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/tree/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9), only **Ticketmaster / Live Nation** links have dedicated, tested support ([`ticketmaster.ts`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/customer/studio/research/ticketmaster.ts), [Discovery API branch](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L523-L546), [`smoke-ticketmaster.mjs`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/scripts/smoke-ticketmaster.mjs), [handoff doc](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/docs/integration/event-intelligence.md)). Every other link, Luma included, goes through the **generic page parse** in live mode only ([`fetchPage`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L68) → [`extract`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L241)). The generic parse reads the first schema.org Event node in JSON-LD and falls back to `og:title` / `<title>`. Demo mode answers non-fixture links with `demo_only`.

What I verified on 2026-10-14 (curl with the app's own `TicketStubResearch/0.1` user agent, and Luma's official help and API docs):

| Behaviour | Evidence | Effect on the current generic path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lu.ma/<slug>` → **301** → `luma.com/<slug>`; `www.luma.com` → 307 → `luma.com`; `help.lu.ma` → `help.luma.com` | live probe | Works, but costs a redirect hop |
| `luma.com/event/evt-…` → 307 → `luma.com/<slug>`; `lu.ma/e/evt-…` → `luma.com/e/evt-…` → … | live probe | `www.lu.ma/e/evt-…` needs **4 hops** to reach the event page, which exceeds [`INTAKE_LIMITS.redirects = 3`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/server/intake-url.ts#L22). **Fails today** with `too_many_redirects` |
| Event pages (for example the neatHack event `luma.com/s5blr882`, see #27) return 200 with an `Event` JSON-LD node: `name`, `startDate`/`endDate` with offset, `location`, `organizer[]`, `offers[]` (price, currency, `availability`), `eventStatus`, `eventAttendanceMode`, `image` on `images.lumacdn.com` | live probe | Name, date and venue are read. **Hosts (`organizer`), end date, status and offers are dropped**. An online event's location is `{"name":"Online","address":"Online"}`, so the parser sets `city = "Online"` and then [requests weather for "Online"](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L604-L611) |
| `luma.com/embed/event/evt-…/simple` returns 200 with the same `Event` node | live probe | Works generically |
| Calendar pages (`luma.com/<calendar>`), city/discover pages (`luma.com/sf`) and profiles (`luma.com/user/…`) return 200 with `Organization`/`Person`, or with events only inside an `ItemList` | live probe | [`collectNodes`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L168-L176) skips `ItemList`, so these fall back to a title-only "event" such as **"Popular events in San Francisco · Events Calendar"** with a guessed date. A **misleading stub, not a refusal** |
| Unknown slug → 404 | live probe | Generic `readError` |
| `luma.com/join/…` is a **per-guest** join link that redirects to the guest's Zoom/online URL ([Luma help](https://help.luma.com/p/zoom-integration)). Messages use `luma.link` and older `o.lu.ma` short links ([Luma help](https://help.luma.com/p/email-delivery-open-troubleshooting)) | Luma docs, probe | Would be fetched like any other link, even though it can carry a guest-specific token |
| Custom URLs live only under `luma.com/<slug>`. Old slugs forward but can later be **claimed by another event**. Luma has **no white-label/custom domains** ([Luma help](https://help.luma.com/p/updating-event-information)) | Luma docs | Recognition can be host-based. A redirected old slug can land on a different event |
| The Luma API (`https://public-api.luma.com`) needs **Luma Plus**, and "each key only grants access to the calendar it was created on" ([Luma API docs](https://docs.luma.com/reference/getting-started-with-your-api)) | Luma docs | **Not usable** for arbitrary customer-pasted events. Dedicated support must be a page/JSON-LD adapter, not an API client |
| `luma.com/robots.txt` has rules only for `Googlebot` | live probe | No disallow for our agent. Terms-of-use review is still pending (see below) |

There is no existing Luma issue in the org. #27 only mentions a Luma page for hackathon registration. Closed [GT-03 #11](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/11) owns generic URL intake. Dedicated provider support is not tracked anywhere.

## Scope

Model this on the Ticketmaster adapter, but use a page/JSON-LD source instead of an API:

- **Recognition (`src/customer/studio/research/luma.ts` or equivalent, no network):** `parseLumaUrl` accepts http(s) hosts `luma.com`, `www.luma.com`, `lu.ma` and `www.lu.ma` (exact hosts, not suffix matches). It classifies the path:
  - **Event:** `/<slug>`, `/e/evt-…`, `/event/evt-…`, `/embed/event/evt-…/…`
  - **Not an event:** calendar, city/discover, `/user/…`, `/create`, `/home` and similar
  - **Private:** `/join/…`
  - **Short link:** `luma.link`, `o.lu.ma`

  Event links are canonicalised to `https://luma.com/…` before fetching, which keeps `www.lu.ma/e/evt-…` within the existing 3-hop limit without raising it. Query strings are dropped from the canonical URL used for fetching, `sourceUrl` and logs (`utm_*` and any token parameters).
- **Routing:** add a Luma branch in `/api/research` next to the Ticketmaster branch, live mode only. It uses the existing `fetchPublic` safe fetch, with every hop still validated. The final URL after redirects must still be a Luma event page, otherwise it gets the "not a single event" refusal. Demo mode keeps returning `demo_only`.
- **Metadata mapping** from the event JSON-LD into `EventData` / `Fact`, with `source: "Luma"`, `sourceUrl` set to the canonical event URL and `provenance: "live"`:
  - title from `name` (the " · Luma" suffix is never part of the title)
  - start date from the event's own local date in `startDate`, plus an end date for multi-day events
  - venue/city from `location` (`Place`/`PostalAddress`)
  - a "Hosted by" fact from `organizer[]`
  - an online/hybrid marker from `eventAttendanceMode` or an "Online" location
  - cancelled/postponed/moved status from `eventStatus`
  - price/availability from `offers[]`

  Online events never trigger a weather lookup for "Online". When registration hides the location, the venue is shown as pending rather than invented. The Luma cover image may be recorded as a reference, but it is never used as stub art without a rights decision.
- **Useful failures** (fixed messages, input never echoed, each one an `intake_rejected`/error `code`):
  - not a single event: "That Luma link is a calendar or profile. Open the event and copy its link."
  - `/join/` and short links, refused **before any fetch**: "That's a personal Luma link. Copy the event page link instead."
  - event not found or removed (404)
  - private or approval-only event with no readable details
  - too many redirects
  - Luma unavailable or blocked (403/429/5xx after the existing retry)
- **Observability and copy:** add `luma` to the `research_started` sources ([`events.ts`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/server/events.ts#L25)), to `SourceName`/`dependency` ([`schema.ts`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/server/observability/schema.ts#L28), [`measure.ts`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/server/observability/measure.ts#L164)), to the help FAQ ([`faq.tsx`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/help/faq.tsx#L41)) and to the input placeholder or examples where appropriate. Check that the [privacy page](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/privacy/page.tsx#L67) list of contacted services stays accurate.
- **Event-intelligence handoff:** record Luma in the source-support matrix ([event-intelligence #7](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence/issues/7)) and give it a source identity (for example `source:luma-event-<evt id or slug>`), matching how [`ticketmasterPackage.ts`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/customer/studio/research/ticketmasterPackage.ts) builds `source_refs`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **URL recognition:** unit tests show `parseLumaUrl` classifies these correctly with no network:
  - **Events:** `luma.com/<slug>`, `lu.ma/<slug>`, `www.luma.com/<slug>`, `www.lu.ma/<slug>`, `/e/evt-…`, `/event/evt-…`, `/embed/event/evt-…/simple`, bare `lu.ma/<slug>` (no scheme), mixed-case hosts, and links with `utm_*` or other query strings
  - **Not events:** calendar, city, `/user/…` and `/create` pages
  - **Private:** `/join/…`, `luma.link/…`, `o.lu.ma/…`
  - **Not Luma:** `luma.ai`, `notluma.com`, `luma.com.evil.example`, `lu.ma.example.com`, plus any link that `parseIntakeUrl` rejects
- [ ] **Redirects:** with a stubbed resolver/fetch, `lu.ma`, `www.lu.ma` and `/e/evt-…` / `/event/evt-…` inputs all reach the event page within `INTAKE_LIMITS.redirects` (3), which stays unchanged. A redirect to a non-Luma or blocked destination is refused. A redirect that ends on a calendar or non-event Luma page gets the "not a single event" refusal, not a title-only stub.
- [ ] **Event metadata:** recorded fixtures (sanitized HTML from a real in-person event, an online event, a multi-day event, a cancelled event, a sold-out/free event and a paid event) produce:
  - the correct title with no " · Luma" suffix
  - start date (and end date when multi-day)
  - venue/city, or an "Online" marker with **no weather lookup**
  - a "Hosted by" fact
  - status and price/availability facts
  - `source: "Luma"`, a canonical `sourceUrl` and confidences documented in the code

  A page whose JSON-LD is missing or malformed falls back to the existing title parse, labelled low-confidence.
- [ ] **Useful failures:**
  - `/join/` and short links are refused before any network request (asserted by a fetch spy)
  - calendar, city and profile pages, 404s, too many redirects and 403/429/5xx each return their own fixed message and `code`
  - none of these echo the input URL or log it with its query string
  - demo mode still returns `demo_only` for Luma links
- [ ] **Coverage:** new `tests/luma*.test.mjs` run offline in `npm test`, plus a `scripts/smoke-luma.mjs` (or an equivalent `verify:product` fixture case) that runs on saved fixtures with no network. Existing Ticketmaster, intake-boundary and research-retry tests still pass. Observability enum tests are updated for the new `luma` source.
- [ ] Help/FAQ copy names Luma as supported only once the above passes. The support matrix entry in event-intelligence is updated or linked.

## Dependencies / related work

- Related: [intake #11](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/11), [bulk link paste #141](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/141) (Luma links should validate and dedupe on their canonical URL there too), [research presentation #12](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/12), [event-intelligence #7](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence/issues/7) and [#9](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence/issues/9) (support matrix and safe retrieval).
- **Owner decision before live use:** review [Luma's terms](https://luma.com/terms) for automated page access and image use. If they restrict it, keep Luma on the generic parse (or disable it) and record that decision.
- Master acceptance IDs: N/A. This is a new post-v1 feature, and its mapping is pending triage.

## Validation plan / evidence required

Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build`. Run the offline Luma smoke script on the saved fixtures. Then do one owner-authorized live-mode check on Preview with a public Luma event, a `lu.ma` short form and a calendar link, recording the sanitized responses. Before closure, attach the PR, the tested commit, fixture provenance and dates, and command results. The probe results above are dated 2026-10-14 and must be re-checked when implementing. Creating this issue does not claim implementation or passing tests.
issues.title: [Post deployment][P2] Support Luma (luma.com / lu.ma) event links with dedicated recognition, metadata and failures

issues.body:
## Summary / user outcome

Links from Ticketmaster-owned platforms that the app does not recognise yet (**Universe**, **FrontGate Tickets** and **TicketWeb**) should resolve through the existing Ticketmaster Discovery integration and produce stubs with the same accuracy as Ticketmaster links.

**Priority:** P2, post-v1. This is the cheapest provider win because the API client, key and mapper already exist. **Required for v1:** No. **Issue key:** new (pending triage). **Owner role:** Product and frontend (research route).

## Geographic coverage (verified 2026-10-14)
<!-- geo-coverage:2026-10-14 -->

Ticketmaster itself is international, including the US ([ticketmaster.com](https://www.ticketmaster.com), [.co.uk](https://www.ticketmaster.co.uk), [.com.au](https://www.ticketmaster.com.au)). Platforms in scope:

| Provider | Classification | Regions evidenced | Official sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Universe | Unverified | Official homepage claims '25 Countries' and support in 19 countries but names none (not even the US) | [www.universe.com](https://www.universe.com) |
| FrontGate | International including US | United States (many states), Mexico (Tijuana, Mexico City), Canada (Saskatchewan, Alberta) | [www.frontgatetickets.com](https://www.frontgatetickets.com) |
| TicketWeb | International including US | United States, Canada (ticketweb.ca), United Kingdom (ticketweb.uk) | [www.ticketweb.com](https://www.ticketweb.com), [www.ticketweb.ca](https://www.ticketweb.ca), [www.ticketweb.uk](https://www.ticketweb.uk) |

Coverage is taken from the providers' own sites, help centres or country domains, checked 2026-10-14. It is not inferred from headquarters. Regions not listed are **unknown**, not excluded. Evidence marked as a snippet was seen through search-indexed copies of official pages because the site blocks direct requests. Priority is unchanged: **P2**, post-v1 / nice to have; **Required for v1:** No.

## Current architecture (shared context)

At [main 3ded858](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/tree/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9), only Ticketmaster / Live Nation links get **dedicated, tested support**. That path is [`ticketmaster.ts`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/customer/studio/research/ticketmaster.ts) (Discovery API v2, host regex `(ticketmaster|livenation).<tld>`) plus [`smoke-ticketmaster.mjs`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/scripts/smoke-ticketmaster.mjs). Every other public link goes through **generic page parsing** in live mode only: [`fetchPage`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L68) (app user agent `TicketStubResearch/0.1`, 8 s timeout, 2 MB cap, at most 3 validated redirects, no JavaScript) → [`extract`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L241). `extract` reads the first schema.org Event-typed JSON-LD node (top level, `@graph` or `subEvent`; not `ItemList`) and otherwise falls back to a low-confidence `og:title` / `<title>`. Demo mode answers non-fixture links with `demo_only`. Luma is tracked separately in #142. Bulk pasting (#141) should validate and dedupe on whatever canonical URL this work defines.

Probe evidence below comes from 2026-10-14. Requests were made from a development machine with curl, using the app's exact user agent and accept header. Bot protection also scores TLS fingerprint and IP address, so results from the production host can differ. Re-check before implementing.

## Exact gap and evidence

| Platform | Domains seen | Today | Official coverage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Universe | `www.universe.com/events/…` | **Confirmed gap.** The event page is a ~2.5 KB JavaScript shell titled "Sell Tickets, Create Events and Discover Experiences - Universe" with no JSON-LD, so the generic parse would create a stub with that title | Discovery `source=universe` |
| FrontGate | `www.frontgatetickets.com/events/{slug}`, per-event storefronts `<event>.frontgatetickets.com`, short link `on.fgtix.com` → 301 → storefront | **Confirmed gap.** No JSON-LD on the pages probed | Discovery `source=frontgate` |
| TicketWeb | `www.ticketweb.com/event/…/{id}` | Generic parse works but is noisy: the `name` is "Tickets for … \| TicketWeb – venue…". One season-pass page had `startDate` 2026-01-01 | Listed as a supported platform; **not** a Discovery `source` value |

Sources: the [Ticketmaster API getting-started page](https://developer.ticketmaster.com/products-and-docs/apis/getting-started/) ("Our APIs work against many platforms including Ticketmaster, TicketWeb, Universe, FrontGate, Ticketmaster Resale (TMR)"). The [Discovery API v2 docs](https://developer.ticketmaster.com/products-and-docs/apis/discovery-api/v2/) list `source` values `ticketmaster`, `universe`, `frontgate`, `tmr`, and the default quota is 5000 calls/day at 5 requests/second. [`isTicketmasterHost`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/customer/studio/research/ticketmaster.ts#L87-L90) only matches `ticketmaster|livenation`, so none of these hosts ever reach Discovery.

## Scope

- Extend recognition (a new `parseTicketmasterFamilyUrl`, or an extension of `parseTicketmasterUrl`) to exact hosts `universe.com`, `www.universe.com`, `frontgatetickets.com`, `www.frontgatetickets.com`, `*.frontgatetickets.com` storefronts and `on.fgtix.com`, plus `ticketweb.com` / `www.ticketweb.com` and any TicketWeb country domains verified during implementation. Extract the platform's event id or slug from each path form.
- Look events up through Discovery: by id where the platform id is a Discovery id, otherwise by keyword/URL match with `source=` set. Record `matchedBy` exactly as the Ticketmaster path does. Map results with the existing mapper. The fact `source` names the platform (for example "Universe via Ticketmaster"), and `sourceUrl` is always the public event URL.
- **Spike first for TicketWeb.** Show whether Discovery returns TicketWeb events (by id or search). If it does not, keep TicketWeb on the generic parse and clean the name instead: strip the "Tickets for" prefix and the "| TicketWeb – …" suffix. Treat pass or season products with no single date as needing review.
- Fallbacks follow the Ticketmaster pattern. With no key, 401/403, 429, timeout or no match, fall through to the page parse. If the page is a JavaScript shell with no event data (Universe), return a specific "we couldn't read this Universe page" failure or the manual-details fallback (see bot-blocked ticketers #144). It must never produce a stub titled with the platform's marketing headline.
- Update observability (`research_started` source, `SourceName`), the help FAQ and the event-intelligence package `source_refs` (`ticketmasterPackage.ts`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests classify Universe, FrontGate (main site, storefront subdomain, `on.fgtix.com`) and TicketWeb URLs, including mixed-case hosts, query strings and lookalike hosts (`universe.com.evil.example`, `notfrontgatetickets.com`), with no network.
- [ ] Saved Discovery fixtures for one Universe and one FrontGate event map to `EventData` with title, date, venue, city, lineup and status. `matchedBy` and the platform source are shown, and `sourceUrl` is the public URL. These run offline in `npm test` and a smoke script.
- [ ] `on.fgtix.com` short links reach a recognised event within `INTAKE_LIMITS.redirects` (3).
- [ ] With no `TICKETMASTER_API_KEY`, or on 429/timeout/no match, the response says why (as the `ticketmaster` meta does today). Universe never yields the "Sell Tickets, Create Events…" title as an event.
- [ ] The TicketWeb spike result is recorded in the PR. Either Discovery lookup is tested, or the generic-parse name cleanup is tested on a saved TicketWeb fixture.
- [ ] Existing Ticketmaster tests and smoke checks still pass. Discovery quota use per request is unchanged: one lookup, no fan-out.

## Dependencies / related work

#142 (Luma, the same adapter pattern), #141 (bulk paste), [event-intelligence #7](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence/issues/7) (support matrix), [`docs/integration/event-intelligence.md`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/docs/integration/event-intelligence.md). A live check needs the owner-held `TICKETMASTER_API_KEY` on Preview.

## Validation plan / evidence required

Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build`. Offline tests use saved, sanitized fixtures and assert that no unexpected network request is made. Live checks happen only on Preview in live mode, with owner authorization, and record their mode. Before closure, attach the PR, the tested commit, fixture provenance and dates, and command results. Creating this issue does not claim implementation or passing tests.

## Dedicated provider issues (triage 2026-10-14)

Universe #157, FrontGate #158. TicketWeb remains tracked here.

At [main 3ded858](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/tree/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9), only Ticketmaster / Live Nation links get **dedicated, tested support**. ## Exact gap and evidence

These providers returned a bot challenge or block to the app's user agent on both the homepage and an event page, unless noted:

| Provider | Domains seen | Probe result | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AXS | `www.axs.com` (including `/au/events/{id}/{slug}` from AXS's sitemap) | 403 Cloudflare challenge (`cf-mitigated: challenge`) | Confirmed gap |
| SeatGeek | `seatgeek.com` (`seatgeek.ca` seen in search, unverified) | 403 DataDome | Confirmed gap |
| StubHub | `www.stubhub.com/{slug}/event/{id}/` | 403 DataDome | Confirmed gap |
| Resident Advisor | `ra.co/events/{id}` (`de.ra.co` seen in search) | 403 DataDome | Confirmed gap |
| See Tickets / Eventim | `www.seetickets.com` (UK); `www.seetickets.us` → 302 → `www.eventim.us`; `www.eventim.de`, `www.eventim.co.uk` | 403 Akamai (UK), 403 Cloudflare (eventim.us), connection reset or a 15 s timeout (eventim.de/.co.uk; the app's limit is 8 s). Event pages not tested | Confirmed gap (homepages) |
| Shotgun | `shotgun.live` | 429 "Vercel Security Checkpoint" on homepage, venue page and sitemap | Confirmed gap |
| Skiddle | `www.skiddle.com/whats-on/{city}/{venue}/{slug}/{id}/` | 202 AWS WAF challenge on the event page | Confirmed gap (API path tracked separately) |
| Etix | `www.etix.com` → `/ticket/` | 202 AWS WAF challenge on the homepage. No event page found | Homepage blocked; event page unverified |
| Tixr | `www.tixr.com` | 403 DataDome on the homepage. No event page found | Homepage blocked; event page unverified |

Today [`fetchPage`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L68) treats a 403/202/429 challenge like any HTTP failure and ends in the generic [`readError`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L435). A 202 challenge page with HTML could even be parsed as a title-only "event". The [event-intelligence support-matrix proposal (#7)](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence/issues/7) already defines `ACCESS_RESTRICTED` with "no bypass". This issue implements the customer-facing side of that rule.

- **Recognition:** add a small provider registry (exact host or host-suffix rules) for the providers above. It is used for messaging and analytics only, not for routing around protection.
- **Detection:** classify challenge responses as `access_restricted`: 403/429 with known challenge markers (`cf-mitigated`, `x-datadome`, Akamai "Unusual Traffic", `x-amzn-waf-action`, Vercel checkpoint) and 202 WAF challenges. They are never parsed as event pages. Timeouts stay `timeout`. **No bypass:** no browser automation, header spoofing or user-agent rotation.
- **Customer outcome:** show a specific message ("AXS doesn't let us read its pages automatically") plus a **manual-details fallback**. The fallback is a short form for event name, date and venue/city, prefilled from the URL slug where one exists (for example a StubHub or RA slug). It produces a stub whose facts are marked `provenance` customer-entered or pending, never "live". Weather and other enrichment can still run from the entered city and date.
- **Official access evaluation (one checklist item per provider):** record whether an official or partner API can read an arbitrary public event by id. Cover the AXS, SeatGeek (developer portal), StubHub, Resident Advisor, Eventim/See Tickets, Shotgun, Etix and Tixr terms, and record a decision for each: adapter issue, fallback only, or not supported. Skiddle's API is tracked in its own issue.

- [ ] Saved challenge responses (Cloudflare 403, DataDome 403, Akamai 403, AWS WAF 202, Vercel 429) are classified `access_restricted` and never reach `extract`. A test proves a 202 challenge page cannot become a title-only stub.
- [ ] For a recognised provider, the response names the provider and offers the manual-details fallback. For an unrecognised blocked host, a generic "this site blocks automated reads" message plus the fallback.
- [ ] Manual fallback: required name and date, optional venue/city; validation and length limits match the intake rules. The resulting stub labels the facts as customer-entered, and weather uses the entered city and date. Works on phone and desktop and is accessible.
- [ ] No retry loop or alternative fetch is attempted after a challenge. Observability records `access_restricted` with the provider id, never the full URL.
- [ ] The official access evaluation table is recorded in the PR or docs, with official links and a decision per provider.

## Dependencies / related work

[event-intelligence #7](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence/issues/7) and [#9](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence/issues/9), [GT-05 #12](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/12) (permission-sensitive blockers), [GT-11 #18](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/18) (accessibility), #141, #142, and Skiddle API #145.

## Validation plan / evidence required

Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build`. Offline tests use saved, sanitized fixtures and assert that no unexpected network request is made. Live checks happen only on Preview in live mode, with owner authorization, and record their mode. Before closure, attach the PR, the tested commit, fixture provenance and dates, and command results. Creating this issue does not claim implementation or passing tests.

## Dedicated provider issues (triage 2026-10-14)

AXS #153, Tixr #154, Resident Advisor #155, Shotgun #159, Etix #164, TicketSource #172, Ticketek #176, EVENTIM / See Tickets #178, Skiddle (API path) #145. SISTIC #179 (also see #153), Klook #181, SeatGeek #182, StubHub North America / viagogo #183, StubHub International #184. No provider in the table above is now covered only here. _Geography note (2026-10-14): StubHub International's [official separation article](https://support.stubhub.ie/en/support/solutions/articles/80000695006-stubhub-business-separation-update) separates StubHub North America (stubhub.com/.ca, owned by viagogo; #183) from StubHub International (19 European sites plus stubhub.mx, Digital Fuel Capital; #184). That supersedes the StubHub row's "rest of world on stubhub.ie" wording; stubhub.com.au is unknown._ Provider-specific scope belongs in the dedicated issues; this issue keeps the shared detection and fallback.

Live checks happen only on Preview in live mode, with owner authorization, and record their mode. Before closure, attach the PR, the tested commit, fixture provenance and dates, and command results. Creating this issue does not claim implementation or passing tests.

Give Eventbrite, the largest community, club and small-venue platform, dedicated and tested support: canonical event ids, all of its country domains, richer facts, and correct handling of Eventbrite pages that are not single events. **Priority:** P2, post-v1. **Required for v1:** No. **Issue key:** new (pending triage). **Owner role:** Product and frontend.

## Geographic coverage (verified 2026-10-14)
<!-- geo-coverage:2026-10-14 -->

**Eventbrite: International including US.** Regions evidenced: US plus 25 country domains: UK, IE, CA, AU, NZ, DE, AT, CH, FR, BE, NL, ES, PT, IT, DK, SE, FI, BR, AR, MX, CL, CO, PE, HK, SG.

- **Official sources:** [www.eventbrite.com](https://www.eventbrite.com/), [www.eventbrite.co.uk](https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/), [www.eventbrite.com.br](https://www.eventbrite.com.br/)
- **Evidence:** eventbrite.com links 26 country sites; .co.uk, .com.au, .de, .com.br and .ca homepages return 200.

Coverage is taken from the providers' own sites, help centres or country domains, checked 2026-10-14. It is not inferred from headquarters. Regions not listed are **unknown**, not excluded. Evidence marked as a snippet was seen through search-indexed copies of official pages because the site blocks direct requests. Priority is unchanged: **P2**, post-v1 / nice to have; **Required for v1:** No.

## Current architecture (shared context)

At [main 3ded858](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/tree/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9), only Ticketmaster / Live Nation links get **dedicated, tested support**. Every other public link goes through **generic page parsing** in live mode only: [`fetchPage`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L68) (app user agent `TicketStubResearch/0.1`, 8 s timeout, 2 MB cap, at most 3 validated redirects, no JavaScript) → [`extract`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L241). `extract` reads the first schema.org Event-typed JSON-LD node (top level, `@graph` or `subEvent`; not `ItemList`) and otherwise falls back to a low-confidence `og:title` / `<title>`. Demo mode answers non-fixture links with `demo_only`. Luma is tracked separately in #142. Bulk pasting (#141) should validate and dedupe on whatever canonical URL this work defines.

Probe evidence below comes from 2026-10-14. Requests were made from a development machine with curl, using the app's exact user agent and accept header. Bot protection also scores TLS fingerprint and IP address, so results from the production host can differ. Re-check before implementing.

## Exact gap and evidence

- **Works generically today (verified):** `www.eventbrite.com/e/{slug}-{id}` returned 200 with a top-level `SocialEvent` JSON-LD node containing name, startDate and venue. `www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/…` → 301 → `.com` (1 hop).
- **Not covered:** no test or fixture guards this, so a markup change on Eventbrite's side would silently degrade results. Organizer, profile, search and city pages are not distinguished from event pages. Eventbrite country domains other than `.co.uk` are unverified. There is no canonical id for deduplication (#141).
- **API:** the [Eventbrite API](https://www.eventbrite.com/platform/api) has `GET /v3/events/{event_id}/` with an OAuth/private token; public event search was shut down in December 2019. It is **unverified** whether a token can read public events the account does not own. Spike this before relying on it.

## Scope

- `eventbrite.ts`: recognise `eventbrite.<tld>` hosts (verify the official country-domain list during implementation) and extract the numeric id from `/e/{slug}-{id}`, `/e/{id}` and checkout/tickets variants. Canonical URL is `https://www.eventbrite.com/e/{id}`.
- Primary read is the JSON-LD page parse with Eventbrite-specific mapping: organizer as "Hosted by", online events (no weather lookup), end date, price/availability and status from `offers` and `eventStatus`. Optionally use the API by id if the spike shows public events are readable, behind a server-only key.
- Non-event Eventbrite pages (organizer `/o/…`, `/d/…` discovery, search) get a specific "open the event and copy its link" refusal, not a title-only stub.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recognition and id-extraction tests cover `.com`, `.co.uk` and the other verified country domains, slug and id forms, query strings, lookalike hosts and non-event paths.
- [ ] Saved fixtures (in-person, online, multi-day, sold-out/free and cancelled events) map to the expected facts, with `source: "Eventbrite"` and the canonical `sourceUrl`. Offline in `npm test`.
- [ ] Organizer and discovery pages are refused with the specific message.
- [ ] The API spike outcome is recorded. If the API is adopted, its no-key/401/429/not-found fallbacks drop back to the page parse, with tests.
- [ ] The canonical id is exposed for deduplication in #141.

## Dependencies / related work

#141, #142, generic-parser hardening #151, [event-intelligence #7](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence/issues/7).

## Validation plan / evidence required

Live checks happen only on Preview in live mode, with owner authorization, and record their mode. Before closure, attach the PR, the tested commit, fixture provenance and dates, and command results. Every other public link goes through **generic page parsing** in live mode only: [`fetchPage`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L68) (app user agent `TicketStubResearch/0.1`, 8 s timeout, 2 MB cap, at most 3 validated redirects, no JavaScript) → [`extract`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L241). `extract` reads the first schema.org Event-typed JSON-LD node (top level, `@graph` or `subEvent`; not `ItemList`) and otherwise falls back to a low-confidence `og:title` / `<title>`. Demo mode answers non-fixture links with `demo_only`. Luma is tracked separately in #142. Bulk pasting (#141) should validate and dedupe on whatever canonical URL this work defines.

Probe evidence below comes from 2026-10-14. Requests were made from a development machine with curl, using the app's exact user agent and accept header. Bot protection also scores TLS fingerprint and IP address, so results from the production host can differ. Re-check before implementing.

## Exact gap and evidence

- **Confirmed gap (no JSON-LD):** `www.facebook.com/events/{id}/` returned 200 with **no JSON-LD**: only `og:title` / `og:description`, with the date in prose. The saved page also contained captcha markers, so served content may vary by request. The generic parse yields a title-only stub with a guessed date at confidence 0.5.
- **Terms:** automated collection from Facebook is governed by Meta's terms, including its Automated Data Collection Terms. Graph API access to events needs page tokens and app review (unverified for this use). **An owner/legal decision is required before any dedicated parsing.**

## Scope

- **Decision step first:** record whether reading public `og:` metadata from a customer-pasted event link is acceptable under Meta's terms, and whether a Graph API path is feasible.
- Recognition: `facebook.com` / `www.facebook.com` / `m.facebook.com` `/events/{id}` forms and verified short links (`fb.me` is unverified). Login walls, groups, profiles and non-event pages are refused specifically.
- **If approved:** an `og:`-based parser for title, date/time from the description text, and venue. Confidences documented; the customer confirms the date.
- **If not approved:** skip fetching and go straight to the manual-details fallback (from bot-blocked ticketers #144), with a message explaining why.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The terms decision is recorded and linked in the PR before any fetching behaviour changes.
- [ ] Recognition tests cover event URL forms, mobile hosts, lookalikes and non-event pages.
- [ ] Approved path: saved fixtures map to title, date and venue with documented confidence; login or captcha pages are detected and never become stubs. Not-approved path: no request is sent to Facebook (asserted by a fetch spy), and the fallback is offered.
- [ ] Offline in `npm test`.

## Dependencies / related work

Bot-blocked ticketers #144 (manual-details fallback), [legal repository](https://github.com/jevelopers-neathack-2026/legal) for the terms decision, #141.

## Validation plan / evidence required

Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build`. Offline tests use saved, sanitized fixtures and assert that no unexpected network request is made. Live checks happen only on Preview in live mode, with owner authorization, and record their mode. Before closure, attach the PR, the tested commit, fixture provenance and dates, and command results. Creating this issue does not claim implementation or passing tests.

## Summary / user outcome

Make generic event-page parsing safer and keep it tested. It must reject pages that list many events instead of picking one at random, clean ticketer boilerplate out of event names, and keep regression fixtures for the platforms that already work through it today: **Vivid Seats, Humanitix, Ticket Tailor, Fever, Songkick** (and TicketWeb if it stays generic).

**Priority:** P2, post-v1. **Required for v1:** No. **Issue key:** new (pending triage). **Owner role:** Product and frontend.

## Geographic coverage (verified 2026-10-14)
<!-- geo-coverage:2026-10-14 -->

| Provider | Classification | Regions evidenced | Official sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vivid Seats | International including US | United States and United Kingdom (resale listings, priced in USD); Canada unverified | [www.vividseats.com/geo/uk/england/london](https://www.vividseats.com/geo/uk/england/london), [www.vividseats.com/geo/uk/concerts](https://www.vividseats.com/geo/uk/concerts) |

| Fever | International including US | US, Canada, Latin America, ~30 European countries, Asia/Middle East, Australia/NZ, South Africa (country selector lists 55 countries) | [feverup.com/en](https://feverup.com/en) |
| Songkick | International including US | US, UK, Germany and other metro areas worldwide (metro selector) | [www.songkick.com/metro-areas/24426-uk-london](https://www.songkick.com/metro-areas/24426-uk-london), [www.songkick.com/metro-areas/28443-germany-berlin](https://www.songkick.com/metro-areas/28443-germany-berlin) |

Coverage is taken from the providers' own sites, help centres or country domains, checked 2026-10-14. It is not inferred from headquarters. Regions not listed are **unknown**, not excluded. Evidence marked as a snippet was seen through search-indexed copies of official pages because the site blocks direct requests. Priority is unchanged: **P2**, post-v1 / nice to have; **Required for v1:** No.

## Current architecture (shared context)

At [main 3ded858](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/tree/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9), only Ticketmaster / Live Nation links get **dedicated, tested support**. That path is [`ticketmaster.ts`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/customer/studio/research/ticketmaster.ts) (Discovery API v2, host regex `(ticketmaster|livenation).<tld>`) plus [`smoke-ticketmaster.mjs`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/scripts/smoke-ticketmaster.mjs). Every other public link goes through **generic page parsing** in live mode only: [`fetchPage`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L68) (app user agent `TicketStubResearch/0.1`, 8 s timeout, 2 MB cap, at most 3 validated redirects, no JavaScript) → [`extract`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L241). `extract` reads the first schema.org Event-typed JSON-LD node (top level, `@graph` or `subEvent`; not `ItemList`) and otherwise falls back to a low-confidence `og:title` / `<title>`. Demo mode answers non-fixture links with `demo_only`. Luma is tracked separately in #142. Bulk pasting (#141) should validate and dedupe on whatever canonical URL this work defines.

Probe evidence below comes from 2026-10-14. Requests were made from a development machine with curl, using the app's exact user agent and accept header. Bot protection also scores TLS fingerprint and IP address, so results from the production host can differ. Re-check before implementing.

## Exact gap and evidence

Platforms where generic parsing works today (probe verified; each returned 200 with a top-level Event-typed node):

| Platform | Event URL form | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vivid Seats | `www.vividseats.com/{slug}/production/{id}` | `SportsEvent` (resale) |
| Humanitix | `events.humanitix.com/{slug}` ([fixed format](https://help.humanitix.com/en/articles/8905545)) | Homepage has only an `ItemList`, correctly not matched |
| Ticket Tailor | `www.tickettailor.com/events/{org}/{id}` | Clean JSON-LD name; page title starts "Select tickets –". `buytickets.at` is unverified |
| Fever | `feverup.com/m/{id}` (`feverup.com` → 301 → `/en`) | `Product` plus top-level `Event` |
| Songkick | `www.songkick.com/concerts/{id}-{slug}` | `MusicEvent`; the [API](https://www.songkick.com/developer) is for paid partners only |

Problems confirmed in the shared parser:

- **Multi-event pages:** [`findJsonLdEvent`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L178-L190) returns the first Event node, so a page listing many events (for example the Meetup homepage) yields an unrelated event. Listing pages that use `ItemList` (Luma city pages) fall back to a title-only "event" titled like "Popular events in San Francisco · Events Calendar".
- **Boilerplate in names:** the title fallback splits only on `|`, `–`, `—` and `-`, not on `·` (Luma). JSON-LD names can contain marketing text, for example "Tickets for … | TicketWeb – venue".
- **Challenge pages:** a 2xx bot-challenge page can pass through to the title fallback.
- **No coverage:** no saved-fixture tests guard the platforms that work today.

## Scope

- Count the distinct top-level Event nodes, plus `ItemList`/`ListItem` events. When a page holds **more than one** distinct event and none matches the page's canonical URL or `@id`, return a specific "this page lists several events. Open one and copy its link" refusal.
- Return the same refusal when the page has an `ItemList` of events but no standalone Event. Never produce a title-only stub from a listing page.
- Clean names: strip known suffixes and prefixes ("Tickets for", "· Luma", "| TicketWeb …", "Select tickets –") through a small, tested rule list, and add `·` to the title-split separators.
- Detect challenge pages on a 2xx response (known markers) and route them to the `access_restricted` outcome from bot-blocked ticketers #144.
- Add sanitized fixtures and tests for Vivid Seats, Humanitix, Ticket Tailor, Fever and Songkick that assert title, date, venue and city. They form a regression suite run in `npm test`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Meetup-homepage-style fixture (several `Event` nodes) and a Luma-city-style fixture (events in an `ItemList`) both return the "lists several events" refusal. A single-event page that also embeds related events still picks the event matching its canonical URL or `@id`.
- [ ] Name cleanup tests cover each rule; legitimate names containing "Tickets" or a pipe are not damaged.
- [ ] A 2xx challenge fixture never becomes a stub.
- [ ] The regression fixtures for the five platforms pass offline, and existing intake-boundary and research-retry tests still pass.
- [ ] Help/FAQ wording stays "any event page with event data". These platforms are not advertised as dedicated integrations.

## Dependencies / related work

#142 (Luma listing pages and `·` titles), Meetup #148, Eventbrite #146, DICE #147, Posh #149, bot-blocked ticketers #144, spike #152, #141.

## Validation plan / evidence required

Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build`. Offline tests use saved, sanitized fixtures and assert that no unexpected network request is made. Live checks happen only on Preview in live mode, with owner authorization, and record their mode. Before closure, attach the PR, the tested commit, fixture provenance and dates, and command results. Creating this issue does not claim implementation or passing tests.

## Dedicated provider issues (triage 2026-10-14)

Ticket Tailor #160, Humanitix #161, Songkick #167, ShowClix / Leap Events #173, Fever #174. Vivid Seats remains covered only here. Provider-specific scope belongs in the dedicated issues; this issue keeps the shared parser hardening and regression suite.

comments.body: Ticket Tailor specifics are in #160: organiser pages (/events/{org}) currently become a stub titled "Buy tickets" through the title fallback, and buytickets.at is a verified 301 alias. Partiful (#156) found another generic-path defect: UTC startDate values (…Z) are cut to their first 10 characters, so evening events in the Americas land on the next day. Any JSON-LD date with an offset or Z should be converted to the event's local date.

Dedicated Humanitix issue: #161. Confirmed defect: a JSON-LD startDate offset that reflects the requester's timezone produces a day-early date (slug says 14 October, the app would record 13 October), and humanitix.com/us becomes a stub titled "Humanitix". Tito #163 shows the date guesser misses ranges such as "July 13–19, 2026".
Dedicated Songkick issue: #167 (Songkick was a regression-fixture row here). ShowClix / Leap Events (#173) parses generically today; its fixture should join this suite.

Triage 2026-10-14: TICKETINO has a dedicated issue, #180. Its pages use an HTML-entity-encoded script type (`application/ld+json`) that the generic JSON-LD matcher misses. Decoding that attribute is a generic fix, so its fixture belongs in this regression suite.

Triage 2026-10-14: two new dedicated issues add regression-suite fixtures here. #185 Moshtix: schema.org event pages with several Event nodes, where the first node isn't guaranteed to be the page's event. #186 Oztix: a JS-shell title using a `·` separator that the title split misses, which creates false stubs.

Triage 2026-10-14: two new dedicated issues add regression-suite fixtures here. #189 Showpass: title-only fallback, with the date found only when the title contains it, plus embedded page data with IANA timezones. #190 Fatsoma (UK and US): schema.org `startDate` values ending in `Z`, where `slice(0,10)` can give the wrong local day.

Triage 2026-10-14: two new dedicated issues add regression-suite fixtures here. #193 Weezevent (`my.weezevent.com`) and #194 District (`district.in` / `district.ae`) both have schema.org pages that parse today. Both use UTC `startDate` values that need local-date conversion instead of `slice(0,10)`, and Weezevent names contain HTML entities.

Triage 2026-10-14: two new dedicated issues add regression-suite fixtures here. #195 Fienta: schema.org with offset dates, plus a home-page title using a `•` separator, which creates a false stub. #197 NOL World: schema.org with date-only multi-day runs and full-width brackets in titles. Both parse today through the generic path.

| Item | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Domains | `axs.com` → 301 → `www.axs.com`. Event paths include `/events/{id}/{slug}` and country prefixes such as `/au/events/{id}/{slug}` (from AXS's sitemap) |
| Homepage, event page, `/terms-of-use` | **403 Cloudflare challenge** (`cf-mitigated: challenge`) for the app's user agent |
| `robots.txt` | 200, readable. Robots rules do not lift the challenge |
| Official data access | No public event API found. AXS points integrations to its partnerships team: [solutions.axs.com/us/partnerships-integrations](https://solutions.axs.com/us/partnerships-integrations/). Third-party partner docs ([MoEngage](https://www.moengage.com/docs/partner-guide/personalize-and-optimize/dynamic-content/events-and-ticketing/axs)) state AXS offers no public discovery API. **Unverified with AXS directly** |

**Classification: confirmed gap (blocked).** Generic parsing cannot read AXS today, and nothing in this issue will try to get around that.

## Scope

- AXS entry in the #144 provider registry: exact hosts `axs.com` and `www.axs.com`, plus country hosts verified during implementation. Extract the event id and slug from `/events/{id}/{slug}` and country-prefixed forms. Non-event paths (`/venues/…`, `/artists/…`, search) are classified separately.
- **No fetch attempt for recognised AXS event links** while AXS is known to be blocked: go straight to the fallback, prefilling the event name from the URL slug (marked customer-confirmable, low confidence). Keep a feature flag so a later approved data source can be switched on.
- AXS-specific copy: "AXS doesn't let us read its event pages automatically. Check these details and we'll make your stub."
- **Partnership decision:** the owner contacts AXS partnerships and records the outcome (approved API with terms, refused, or no reply). Only an approved, documented data source may replace the fallback, under a follow-up issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recognition tests: `axs.com`, `www.axs.com`, country-prefixed event paths, query strings, uppercase hosts, lookalikes (`axs.com.evil.example`, `notaxs.com`) and non-event AXS paths.
- [ ] A recognised AXS event link produces the AXS message and a fallback form prefilled from the slug. A fetch spy proves no request is made to `axs.com`.
- [ ] A saved Cloudflare challenge response for an **unrecognised** AXS path is classified `access_restricted` (through #144) and never reaches `extract`.
- [ ] The resulting stub labels its facts as customer-entered; nothing claims "live" AXS data.
- [ ] The partnership enquiry outcome is recorded here with date and evidence. No scraping service, browser automation or header spoofing is introduced.

## Validation plan / evidence required

Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build`. Offline tests use saved, sanitized fixtures and assert that no unexpected network request is made. Live checks happen only on Preview in live mode, with owner authorization, and record their mode. Before closure, attach the PR, the tested commit, fixture provenance and dates, and command results. Creating this issue does not claim implementation or passing tests.

Give Partiful (`partiful.com`) party invites dedicated support. Public Partiful events should produce accurate stubs: the correct **local** date, the host, and a city or venue without exposing a private home address. Private or invite-only links should get a clear message.

<!-- geo-coverage:2026-10-14 -->

**Partiful: International including US.** Regions evidenced: US and 'around the world' (help center names Berlin, Sydney, Rio, Seoul); country list not published.

- **Official sources:** [help.partiful.com/hc/en-us/articles/26526467907611-Where-do-Partiful-parties-happen](https://help.partiful.com/hc/en-us/articles/26526467907611-Where-do-Partiful-parties-happen), [help.partiful.com/hc/en-us/articles/26505680245275-What-are-guest-phone-numbers-used-for](https://help.partiful.com/hc/en-us/articles/26505680245275-What-are-guest-phone-numbers-used-for)
- **Evidence:** 'throughout the U.S. and around the world'; 'We support most international phone numbers.'

Coverage is taken from the providers' own sites, help centres or country domains, checked 2026-10-14. It is not inferred from headquarters. Regions not listed are **unknown**, not excluded. Evidence marked as a snippet was seen through search-indexed copies of official pages because the site blocks direct requests. Priority is unchanged: **P2**, post-v1 / nice to have; **Required for v1:** No.

## Current architecture (shared context)

At [main 3ded858](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/tree/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9), only Ticketmaster / Live Nation links get **dedicated, tested support**. Every other public link goes through **generic page parsing** in live mode only: [`fetchPage`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L68) (app user agent `TicketStubResearch/0.1`, 8 s timeout, 2 MB cap, at most 3 validated redirects, no JavaScript) → [`extract`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L241). `extract` reads the first schema.org Event-typed JSON-LD node (top level, `@graph` or `subEvent`; not `ItemList`) and otherwise falls back to a low-confidence `og:title` / `<title>`. Demo mode answers non-fixture links with `demo_only`. Luma is tracked separately in #142. Bulk pasting (#141) should validate and dedupe on whatever canonical URL this work defines.

Probe evidence below comes from 2026-10-14. Requests were made from a development machine with curl, using the app's exact user agent and accept header. Bot protection also scores TLS fingerprint and IP address, so results from the production host can differ. Re-check before implementing.

## Verified facts (2026-10-14)

| Item | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Domains | `partiful.com`; `www.partiful.com` → 308 → `partiful.com`. Event URLs are `partiful.com/e/{eventId}` |
| Public event pages (2 probed) | **200**, with a top-level `Event` JSON-LD node containing `name`, `startDate`, `endDate` (on one), `location` (Place with full `PostalAddress` including street), `organizer[]`, `eventStatus`, `eventAttendanceMode`, `image` and `description` |
| Unknown event id | 404 |
| `robots.txt` | Allows named search and link-preview bots and disallows AI-training crawlers. It has **no `*` group**, so it does not address our agent. Partiful's [terms](https://partiful.com/terms) need review |
| Official API | None found. [Help center](https://help.partiful.com/) confirms public events exist; RSVPs require a verified phone number |

**Generic parsing works today for public events (verified), with two confirmed defects:**

1. **Wrong date:** `startDate` is UTC (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`), and generic parsing takes the first 10 characters. An evening event in the Americas therefore lands on the **next day**.
2. **Privacy:** the full street address of what is often a private home is exposed to the stub and facts. A keepsake should show the city or venue name, not a home address, unless the customer chooses otherwise.

**Unverified (not tested failures):** invite-only and private events, guest-approval events, password or "RSVP to see address" events, and app-only links. No such link was available, and none should be obtained without permission.

## Scope

- `partiful.ts`: recognise `partiful.com/e/{id}` (and `www.` form); host `/u/…` profiles and other paths are non-events.
- Map JSON-LD to `EventData`:
  - **Date:** convert UTC `startDate`/`endDate` to the event's local date using the address's region or timezone. If the timezone cannot be determined, show the date as needing confirmation with the adjacent-day alternative.
  - **Host:** `organizer` becomes "Hosted by".
  - **Status:** from `eventStatus` and `eventAttendanceMode`.
- **Address privacy:** keep the street address out of facts and stub text by default; use the venue `name` if it is not an address, otherwise the city or region. Weather may use the city.
- Private, invite-only or 404 pages get a specific message: "This Partiful invite is private. Ask the host for the details or enter them yourself", plus the manual-details fallback from #144.
- Record the terms review before advertising Partiful support.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recognition tests: `/e/{id}` with and without `www.`, query strings, lookalikes and non-event paths.
- [ ] Saved fixtures (sanitized, synthetic personal data): an evening event in US Pacific time whose UTC date is the next day maps to the **correct local date**; a multi-day event maps both dates; a cancelled event shows its status.
- [ ] Street address never appears in facts or stub text by default; city/region and non-address venue names do. Covered by tests.
- [ ] A 404 and a private-invite fixture each return the Partiful-specific message and the fallback.
- [ ] Unverified private-event behaviour stays documented as unverified until tested with a host-provided link.
- [ ] Terms review recorded. Offline in `npm test`.

## Validation plan / evidence required

Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build`. Offline tests use saved, sanitized fixtures and assert that no unexpected network request is made. Live checks happen only on Preview in live mode, with owner authorization, and record their mode. Before closure, attach the PR, the tested commit, fixture provenance and dates, and command results. | Item | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Domains | `universe.com` → 301 → `www.universe.com` |
| Event URL form | `www.universe.com/events/{slug}-tickets-{CODE}` (for example `…/events/dinner-cruise-with-live-music-tickets-SNKB2`, from Universe's own `sitemap/listings.xml`) |
| Event page with the app's user agent | **200 but only a 2,487-byte JavaScript shell**: no JSON-LD and the title "Sell Tickets, Create Events and Discover Experiences - Universe". Re-confirmed on a current listing |

| Official coverage | [Discovery API v2](https://developer.ticketmaster.com/products-and-docs/apis/discovery-api/v2/) `source=universe`; [getting started](https://developer.ticketmaster.com/products-and-docs/apis/getting-started/) lists Universe as covered |
| Uncertain | Whether the `{CODE}` suffix maps directly to a Discovery event id or needs a keyword/URL search. No live Discovery call was made (no key on the development machine) |

## Scope

- Universe recogniser (host `universe.com` / `www.universe.com`) that extracts slug and `{CODE}` from `/events/{slug}-tickets-{CODE}`. Other paths (`/users/…`, `/explore`, listing pages) are non-events.
- **Spike:** with the owner-held key on Preview, determine how a Universe listing maps to Discovery (by id, or `keyword` plus `source=universe`), and record the result. Then implement the lookup through the #143 plumbing. `source` is "Universe via Ticketmaster" and `sourceUrl` is the public Universe URL.
- **Never fall back to the JavaScript shell title.** If Discovery cannot match, return a Universe-specific "couldn't find this Universe event" result with the manual-details fallback (#144), with the name prefilled from the slug.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recognition tests: listing URL forms, query strings, uppercase hosts, lookalikes and non-event paths.
- [ ] The spike result (id mapping or search strategy) is recorded with a sanitized live response.
- [ ] Saved Discovery fixtures map to title, date, venue and city with `matchedBy` recorded. Offline in `npm test`.
- [ ] A saved JavaScript-shell fixture can never produce a stub titled "Sell Tickets, Create Events…". This is the regression test for today's defect.
- [ ] No key, 429 and no match each give an explicit outcome and the slug-prefilled fallback.

## Validation plan / evidence required

Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build`. Offline tests use saved, sanitized fixtures and assert that no unexpected network request is made. Live checks happen only on Preview in live mode, with owner authorization, and record their mode. Before closure, attach the PR, the tested commit, fixture provenance and dates, and command results. Creating this issue does not claim implementation or passing tests.

| Item | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Domains | `shotgun.live` and `www.shotgun.live` |
| Homepage, `/en/events`, `sitemap.xml`, venue page | **429 with `x-vercel-mitigated: challenge`** ("Vercel Security Checkpoint") for the app's user agent |

## Summary / user outcome

Support TicketLeap event links (`ticketleap.com` and its event domains). TicketLeap's buyer pages are rendered client-side with no structured data, so today they produce a generic title or a 404 instead of a stub.

## Geographic coverage (verified 2026-10-14)
<!-- geo-coverage:2026-10-14 -->

_Revised 2026-10-14 (triage): claims based only on currency, payment processors or redirects are marked provisional or unverified._

**TicketLeap: Provisional: US plus international (Canada, Australia).** Regions evidenced: United States, Canada, Australia (provisional; from currency and payout support only).

- **Official sources:** [www.ticketleap.com/info/pricing](https://www.ticketleap.com/info/pricing/), [www.ticketleap.com/legal/ticketing-services-agreement](https://www.ticketleap.com/legal/ticketing-services-agreement/)
- **Evidence:** The official pricing FAQ supports sales in the standard currencies of, and payouts to bank accounts in, the United States, Canada and Australia. That is payment support, not an event-coverage statement, so the classification is provisional until an official coverage statement or observed event listings confirm it.

Coverage is taken from the providers' own sites, help centres or country domains, checked 2026-10-14. It is not inferred from headquarters. Regions not listed are **unknown**, not excluded. Evidence marked as a snippet was seen through search-indexed copies of official pages because the site blocks direct requests. **Provisional** means the evidence is only currency, payment-processor or redirect based, so it does not establish event coverage. Priority is unchanged: **P2**, post-v1 / nice to have; **Required for v1:** No.

## Current architecture (shared context)

At [main 3ded858](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/tree/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9), only Ticketmaster / Live Nation links get **dedicated, tested support**. That path is [`ticketmaster.ts`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/customer/studio/research/ticketmaster.ts) (Discovery API v2, host regex `(ticketmaster|livenation).<tld>`) plus [`smoke-ticketmaster.mjs`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/scripts/smoke-ticketmaster.mjs). Every other public link goes through **generic page parsing** in live mode only: [`fetchPage`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L68) (app user agent `TicketStubResearch/0.1`, 8 s timeout, 2 MB cap, at most 3 validated redirects, no JavaScript) → [`extract`](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/3ded8581283ba0890b77659c996c1cee107c6cf9/src/app/api/research/route.ts#L241). `extract` reads the first schema.org Event-typed JSON-LD node (top level, `@graph` or `subEvent`; not `ItemList`) and otherwise falls back to a low-confidence `og:title` / `<title>`. Demo mode answers non-fixture links with `demo_only`. Luma is tracked separately in #142. Bulk pasting (#141) should validate and dedupe on whatever canonical URL this work defines.

Probe evidence below comes from 2026-10-14. Requests were made from a development machine with curl, using the app's exact user agent and accept header. Bot protection also scores TLS fingerprint and IP address, so results from the production host can differ. Re-check before implementing.

## Verified facts (2026-10-14)

| Item | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Marketing site | `ticketleap.com` → 301 → `www.ticketleap.com` (200) |
| Buyer and event host | `events.ticketleap.com`. The **`www.ticketleap.events`** host used in TicketLeap's [help center](https://support.ticketleap.com/) → 301 → `events.ticketleap.com`. The bare `ticketleap.events` does not resolve. The organiser admin is `admin.ticketleap.com` / `admin.ticketleap.events` (not customer links) |
| Organiser storefront | `events.ticketleap.com/events/{org}`: 200, about 11 KB, a JavaScript app shell with **no JSON-LD and no event links** in the HTML. The generic title fallback would yield "{Org} Events Home" as an "event". Confirmed false positive |
| Event page form | The storefront's client bundle builds event links as **`/tickets/{listing_slug}`** on `events.ticketleap.com`. This comes from code inspection, **not from a live event page** |
| Unknown listing | `/tickets/{missing}` → 301 → `/events/{missing}` → 404 "Page Not Found". `www.ticketleap.events/tickets/{missing}` takes 2 hops to the same 404 |
| Not yet verified (implementation tasks) | A real `/tickets/{listing_slug}` page's status and data (JSON-LD, `og:`, or JavaScript-only); legacy `{org}.ticketleap.com/{event}/` URLs; any official buyer-facing API (none found) |

**Classification: storefront pages confirmed unusable for generic parsing; event-page behaviour unknown (must be verified first).**

## Scope

- **Verification task first:** obtain at least one real public `events.ticketleap.com/tickets/{listing_slug}` URL from an organiser's published link. Record its status, redirects and data, and check whether legacy `{org}.ticketleap.com` links still exist. Do not use undocumented private APIs.
- `ticketleap.ts`: recognise `events.ticketleap.com` and `www.ticketleap.events` (canonicalised to `events.ticketleap.com`, which keeps the 2-hop chain to one hop), plus verified legacy forms. `/tickets/{slug}` is an event; `/events/{org}` is an organiser storefront and is refused; `/my-tickets`, `/receipt` and admin hosts are refused as private.
- If event pages carry structured or `og:` data, map it. If they are JavaScript-only, return a TicketLeap-specific message with the manual-details fallback from #144, prefilled from the slug. Never produce a stub from a storefront or app-shell title.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The verification result for a real event page is recorded here (date, status, data), and the chosen mapping or fallback is justified by it.
- [ ] Recognition tests: `/tickets/{slug}` on both hosts, `www.ticketleap.events` canonicalisation, the `/events/{org}` storefront refusal, private `/my-tickets` and admin hosts, lookalikes.
- [ ] A storefront fixture never yields a stub titled "… Events Home".
- [ ] A missing listing (404) returns a specific "this TicketLeap event wasn't found" message.
- [ ] Offline in `npm test`.
